standard_prerequisites.name: The factorization of an immersion as an open immersion followed by a closed immersion, in the quasi-compact case and in the reduced case, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the closed intermediate scheme Z-bar-one inside which the source sits as an open subscheme.

standard_prerequisites.name: The scheme theoretic image of a morphism as the smallest closed subscheme through which it factors, and its density properties in the quasi-compact case, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Places the scheme theoretic image inside the intermediate closed subscheme and supplies scheme theoretic and topological density.

standard_prerequisites.name: A closed immersion into a reduced scheme that is a bijection on underlying topological spaces is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the intermediate closed subscheme with the scheme theoretic image in the reduced case.

core_obligations: Factor the immersion: by the cited factorization results there is a factorization of the immersion into an open immersion followed by a closed immersion, and the scheme theoretic image sits inside the intermediate closed subscheme because the source factors through it (proof lines 3365-3370).

Get the open immersion statement: since the source is an open subscheme of the intermediate closed subscheme and the scheme theoretic image is a closed subscheme of it containing the source, the source is an open subscheme of the scheme theoretic image as well (proof lines 3370-3373).

Reduced case: the source is topologically dense in the intermediate closed subscheme by the construction used in the cited factorization lemma, so that subscheme and the scheme theoretic image have the same topological space, and a closed immersion into a reduced scheme that is bijective on points is an isomorphism; hence the source is scheme theoretically dense in the scheme theoretic image (proof lines 3374-3381).

Quasi-compact case: the scheme theoretic density and the topological density of the source in the scheme theoretic image follow directly from the two cited parts of the quasi-compact scheme theoretic image lemma (proof lines 3382-3387).
proof_roadmap: Factor the immersion into an open immersion followed by a closed immersion and compare the intermediate closed subscheme with the scheme theoretic image (proof lines 3365-3373).

In the reduced case identify the two closed subschemes by density and reducedness, and in the quasi-compact case invoke the density parts of the quasi-compact scheme theoretic image lemma (proof lines 3374-3387).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an immersion which is either quasi-compact or has reduced source, the induced morphism from the source to its scheme theoretic image is an open immersion identifying the source with a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme, and topologically dense as well (statement lines 1355-1363). The counted proof treats the two hypotheses separately: it factors the immersion into an open immersion followed by a closed immersion, uses minimality of the scheme theoretic image to place it inside the intermediate closed subscheme, and then either identifies the two closed subschemes by density together with reducedness and the criterion that a pointwise bijective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism, or quotes the two density assertions for the quasi-compact case (proof lines 1365-1387). It is H2: the case analysis is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are the factorization and density statements of the same chapter.
